:::{#cor-best-predictor-argmin}
#### Conditional mean as the minimizer of squared-error risk

Let $\Predvar$ and $\Outvar$ be [jointly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-jointly-distributed) random variables with $\E{\Outvar^2} < \infty$.
Among [prediction functions](#def-prediction) $\predfnf{\Predvar}$ with $\E{\predfnf{\Predvar}^2} < \infty$,
the [conditional expectation function](#def-cond-expectation-function) is a minimizer of the [squared-error risk](#def-risk):

$$\E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar} \in \argmin_{\predfn} \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \predfnf{\Predvar}}},$$

where $\argmin$ is the [set of minimizers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-argmin).
Moreover, every $\predfn$ in that set satisfies $\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}) = 1$,
so the minimizer is unique up to probability-$1$ equality.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-best-predictor, $\bestpredfnf{\Predvar} = \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}$ has risk no larger than that of any $\predfn$,
so it is a minimizer.
If $\predfn$ is also a minimizer, its risk equals that of $\bestpredfn$,
so the equality case of @thm-best-predictor gives $\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}) = 1$.

:::
